name: Renvael Soursop-Sumac Fizz
description: A sparkling soda that pairs synth-soursop with real sumac extract, producing a drink that is simultaneously tropical and deeply tart. Renvael produces in limited quantities and does not advertise — distribution is word of mouth and a small registered retail list.
flavor_profile: Creamy soursop sweetness up front, then a sharp lemony-astringent sumac tartness that builds rapidly, finishing with a mouth-coating sourness that lingers pleasantly
slogan: We don't need you to find us.
cultural_context: Renvael is the soda equivalent of a restaurant with no sign. Its exclusivity is structural, not performative — they genuinely don't have the capacity to scale. In Tier 3-4 food communities it functions as a social currency: knowing where to get it, and being able to get it, signals a certain kind of connected insider status.
story_hooks: Renvael's registered retail list has a six-month waitlist for new stores — someone is selling slots on that waitlist illegally, and Renvael's two-person operation has no idea how to stop it

A Tier 5 Spire resident has been sending a personal assistant to queue at one of the three shops that stocks Renvael every week — the assistant has started buying extra for herself and selling it at markup to Tier 4 neighbors

Renvael's sumac supplier has just been classified as a protected agricultural heritage source by the city council — a designation that was lobbied for by an anonymous donor, and which will make the ingredient significantly more expensive and harder to access for everyone except whoever controls the heritage license
